title: Two pumps, one beat
style: documentary photograph, anatomical museum specimen, low warm lamp light, muted colour, fine grain, no text, no watermark
negative: text, letters, words, watermark, logo, cartoon, cgi, painting, illustration, modern medical equipment, gore

lines.vo: Your heart is not one pump. It is two, side by side, beating together.
lines.image: an anatomical heart specimen under museum glass

lines.vo: The right side sends blood to the lungs. The left sends it everywhere else.
lines.image: a dark anatomical plate of the chest cavity

lines.vo: The left has to reach your whole body, so its wall is three times thicker.
lines.image: a cross section of cardiac muscle wall

lines.vo: Four chambers. Four valves. Every one of them opens in a single direction.
lines.image: a dissected heart valve, pale tissue

lines.vo: The beat starts on its own. A knot of cells in the right atrium fires.
lines.image: dark tissue lit from one side

lines.vo: The signal spreads, the upper chambers squeeze, then a tenth of a second later the lower.
lines.image: an old oscilloscope trace on dark glass

lines.vo: That delay is the whole trick. Fill first, then fire.
lines.image: a single lamp over dark instruments

lines.vo: About one hundred thousand beats a day, with nobody paying any attention.
Two and a half billion beats in a life, and not one of them is voluntary.
lines.image: an empty examination room at night
lines.title: TWO POINT FIVE BILLION
lines.footer: beats, none of them yours to make
